hypothesis: Coffee is a tree crop: supply answers to price with a delay of years, so price trends continue. The sign of the 12-month return (time-series momentum) tells the direction of the next quarter.
change: Unfitted rule on one feature: buy early if the 252-session return is above zero, else buy late.
expect: RATIO above B3 (63-session momentum) and above zero.

hypothesis: The term structure shows scarcity. In backwardation (near contract above the next one) stocks are tight and a futures buyer earns the roll yield; in contango the price of a contract falls toward spot. The roll-day price gap of the front-month chain measures this slope.
change: Unfitted rule on one feature: carry = minus the mean raw log return of the last 4 roll days. Buy early if carry > 0, else buy late.
expect: Mostly 'buy late' (coffee is usually in contango). RATIO above zero and above always-late.

change: Unfitted rule on one feature: carry = minus the mean raw log return of the last 4 roll days. Buy early if carry > 0, else buy late.

hypothesis: The term structure shows scarcity. In backwardation stocks are tight and the price of a contract rises toward spot; in contango it falls toward spot. The gap between contracts is the raw return of the session after each marked roll day.
change: Unfitted rule on one feature: carry = minus the mean of the last 4 contract gaps. Buy early if carry > 0, else buy late.
expect: Mostly 'buy late' before 2021. RATIO above always-late (+0.06).

hypothesis: Coffee supply and demand answer slowly to price: a high price brings more planting and care and a low price brings neglect, so the price moves back toward its long-run level (commodity 'value').
change: Unfitted rule on one feature: log raw front-month price minus its 5-year mean (1,260 sessions). Buy early if below the mean, else buy late.
expect: RATIO above zero in both halves.

hypothesis: A rain deficit in the Brazilian coffee regions reduces the next crop. The market learns the size of the loss slowly (crop surveys come months later), so the price continues to rise after a dry period.
change: Unfitted rule on one alt-data feature: Brazil output-weighted rain z-score, mean of the last 90 days (at t-4 days). Buy early if below zero, else buy late.
expect: RATIO above zero in both halves.

hypothesis: Coffee trees lose yield when a period is hot and dry at the same time. Stress against the recent climate (not against 1981) is the news. The crop loss enters the price slowly.
change: Unfitted rule on one alt-data feature: Brazil (temperature z - rain z), mean of 90 days, minus its trailing 5-year mean, at t-4 days. Buy early if above zero, else buy late.
expect: Early on about half of the days. RATIO above zero in both halves.

hypothesis: When speculators hold an extreme net position, few buyers (or sellers) remain, and the position must be closed later. An extreme net long position is followed by lower prices, an extreme net short by higher prices.
change: Unfitted three-state rule on one alt-data feature: managed-money net share of open interest, z-score against its last 104 weekly reports. z > +1: buy late. z < -1: buy early. Else steady.
expect: Active on about a third of the days. RATIO above zero.

hypothesis: La Nina brings dry conditions to southern Brazil and El Nino brings rain. The ENSO state is known months before the crop effect, so it can lead the weather stress.
change: Unfitted three-state rule on one alt-data feature: Nino 3.4 anomaly (published value). Below -0.5 (La Nina): buy early. Above +0.5 (El Nino): buy late. Else steady.
expect: RATIO above zero. Active on about half of the days.

hypothesis: If heat-and-dry stress in Brazil enters the price slowly, the same stress in the other arabica origins (about half of world output) must do the same.
change: Same unfitted rule as c06, but the feature is the mean stress of all origins except Brazil (simple mean of country means, 90 days, drift removed).
expect: RATIO above zero, lower than c06. A positive result supports a world stress signal.

hypothesis: Frost in the Brazilian regions destroys part of the next crop. It is a supply shock that the heat-and-dry measure cannot see, and the size of the loss is known only weeks later.
change: c06 plus one feature: buy early if a frost day (lowest regional minimum below 5 C, Jun-Aug) occurred in the last 90 days; else the c06 stress rule.
expect: Few days change. RATIO equal to or above c06.

hypothesis: Root-zone soil moisture is what the tree feels: it sums rain, heat and evaporation over weeks. A dry root zone against the recent seasonal normal means a smaller crop, and the price learns it slowly.
change: Unfitted rule on one alt-data feature from new source 1: Brazil output-weighted root-zone soil wetness, mean of 90 days minus the seasonal normal of the last 5 years, at t-4 days. Buy early if below zero, else buy late.
expect: RATIO above zero in both halves, similar to c06.

hypothesis: Heat-and-dry stress and root-zone soil moisture are two noisy measures of one state (drought stress of the trees). When they agree, the state is clear; when they disagree, there is no information.
change: c06 plus soil moisture as a confirmation (three-state rule): buy early if stress > 0 and soil moisture anomaly < 0; buy late if stress < 0 and soil moisture anomaly > 0; else steady.
expect: Active on about 70% of days. RATIO above c06.

hypothesis: Coffee is priced in dollars. A rising dollar lowers the dollar price of commodities, and currency trends continue for months. A rising dollar index says: wait.
change: Unfitted rule on one market feature from new source 2: 63-session log return of the US dollar index (through t-1). Buy late if above zero, else buy early.
expect: RATIO above zero. Independent of the weather signal.

hypothesis: Brazilian growers sell coffee in dollars and pay costs in reais. When the real weakens, they sell more and accept lower dollar prices. Currency trends continue, so a weakening real says: wait.
change: Unfitted rule on one market feature: 63-session log return of USD/BRL (through t-1). Buy late if above zero (real weaker), else buy early.
expect: RATIO above zero and above the dollar index rule (c13).

hypothesis: The weather signal is strong and the others are weak but independent. Weights fitted on earlier data can use the size of each signal, which a sign rule ignores.
change: Model change: logistic regression (C = 1, scaled) on 4 features: Brazil stress, Brazil soil moisture anomaly, other-origin stress, dollar index 63-session return. Buy early if probability > 0.5, else late.
expect: RATIO near or above c06.

hypothesis: The effect of weather stress can depend on the season and on the state of the market. A random forest averages many shallow trees and can find such conditions with low variance.
change: Model change: random forest (500 trees, depth 4, 50 rows in a leaf, mean of 5 seeds) on 16 features: 6 weather, 7 price, 2 currency, 1 ENSO.
expect: RATIO above the logistic model (c15). A value above c06 would show useful conditions.

hypothesis: Same idea as c16 (the weather effect depends on season and market state), with boosted trees and with all the training years from 2001.
change: Model change: LightGBM (300 trees, depth 3, learning rate 0.03, row share 0.8, column share 0.5, 50 rows in a leaf, mean of 5 seeds) on 15 features (the 16 of c16 without USD/BRL).
expect: RATIO above c16. A value above c06 would show useful conditions.

hypothesis: The crop is made from flowering to grain fill (Sep-Apr). Stress adds up over this season, and stress values of the dry season (May-Aug) are noise. The stress of the season to date is the correct state.
change: c06 with a different time window: mean stress from 1 October to date (growing months Oct-Apr; the last value is held from May to the next October), minus the same quantity of the last 5 years. Same sign rule.
expect: Fewer position changes than c06. RATIO above c06.

hypothesis: Water deficit is the main cause of yield loss in Brazilian arabica. If the signal is drought, the rain part alone carries it and the temperature part adds noise.
change: c18 with the temperature part removed: season-to-date rain deficit (minus rain z), Oct-Apr, minus the same quantity of the last 5 years. Buy early if the deficit is above normal.
expect: RATIO near c18. Clearly lower means that heat matters too.

hypothesis: Heat in the growing season damages flowers and speeds up fruit growth with less bean mass. c19 showed that rain alone is weaker than the combination. Heat alone shows how much of the signal is temperature.
change: c18 with the rain part removed: season-to-date temperature z (Oct-Apr), minus the same quantity of the last 5 years. Buy early if above normal.
expect: RATIO above zero and below c18 (both parts have value).

hypothesis: Heat damage to coffee flowers and fruit comes from hot afternoons. The daily maximum temperature measures this more directly than the mean temperature z-score.
change: c20 with a different heat measure: season-to-date mean of the daily maximum temperature (Brazil, output-weighted, Oct-Apr, held May-Sep), minus the same quantity of the last 5 years. Buy early if above normal.
expect: RATIO equal to or above c20.

hypothesis: Season heat is the state of the crop and the 90-day stress is the recent news. When the news agrees with the state the signal is clear; when they disagree the state is changing and there is no clear call.
change: Agreement rule of two features: buy early if season maximum-temperature anomaly > 0 and 90-day stress > 0; buy late if both < 0; else steady.
expect: Active on about 70% of days. RATIO above c21.

hypothesis: The signal is a slow state of the crop. If that is true, weather data that are 10 days old must give nearly the same result as data that are 4 days old. (Robustness check: real-time POWER values can be late.)
change: c22 with the weather lag changed from 4 to 10 calendar days. Nothing else changes.
expect: RATIO within 0.05 of c22. A large fall would show a fragile result.

hypothesis: The signal is heat against the recent normal. If that is true, a 10-year normal must give a similar result to the 5-year normal. (Robustness check of the one free choice in the season measure.)
change: c22 with the normal of the season maximum temperature changed from the last 5 years to the last 10 years. Nothing else changes.
expect: RATIO within 0.1 of c22.

hypothesis: Roasters substitute between arabica and robusta. A wide arabica premium moves demand to robusta and the arabica price falls back; a narrow premium does the opposite.
change: Unfitted rule on one market feature from new source 3: log(arabica price / robusta price), World Bank monthly, minus its mean of the last 60 months. Buy late if above the mean, else buy early.
expect: RATIO above zero. Independent of weather.

hypothesis: Arabica has a two-year cycle: the branches that grow in one season carry the fruit of the next. Heat in the previous season lowers the coming crop too, so the state must remember it.
change: c22 with the season heat replaced by the mean of this season's and the previous season's maximum-temperature anomaly. Nothing else changes.
expect: RATIO equal to or above c22, with fewer position changes.

hypothesis: Sugar and arabica share Brazil: the same currency, the same weather belt and the same investors. A sugar price trend shows the common Brazil factor before it is complete in coffee.
change: Unfitted rule on one market feature from new source 4: 126-session log return of ICE sugar (through t-1). Buy early if above zero, else buy late.
expect: RATIO above zero. Weak prior.

hypothesis: The weather rule (supply news) and the sugar trend (common Brazil and fund factor) are independent views. A vote of two independent signals with skill has less noise than each one.
change: c22 plus the sugar trend as an equal vote: position = sign(weather agreement position + sign of the 126-session sugar return). Disagreement gives steady; when weather is steady, sugar decides.
expect: RATIO above c22 if the savings are independent.

hypothesis: When world coffee stocks are low against use, there is no buffer and prices tend to rise; with high stocks they tend to fall. Stocks change slowly, so a value that is 1-2 years old still has meaning.
change: Unfitted rule on one alt-data feature from new source 5: world ending stocks / consumption (USDA PSD), minus the mean of the 5 marketing years before; used 12 months after the marketing year ended. Buy early if below that mean, else buy late.
expect: RATIO above zero. Weak prior (old data).

hypothesis: Three signals showed skill with different mechanisms or time scales: season heat (state of the crop), 90-day stress (recent news), sugar trend (common Brazil and fund factor). A majority of three uses all of them and is never without a call.
change: Majority vote of three sign rules: season maximum-temperature anomaly > 0, 90-day stress > 0, 126-session sugar return > 0. Two or three 'yes' -> buy early, else buy late.
expect: RATIO near c22 and c28, with more active days.

hypothesis: Farm commodities share macro demand, the dollar and fund flows. Coffee follows this common factor with a delay. The share of farm markets in an up-trend measures the factor better than sugar alone.
change: Vote of 5 market features: 126-session log return > 0 for sugar, cocoa, cotton, corn, soybeans (through t-1). Three or more rising: buy early, else buy late.
expect: RATIO above the sugar rule (c27, +0.336), equal in the two halves.

hypothesis: Sugar helps and other farm markets do not, so the shared cause is Brazil. Brazilian assets in dollars (equities and the real) rise when capital flows to Brazil, and Brazilian export prices follow.
change: Unfitted rule on one market feature: 126-session log return of the Brazil equity fund EWZ in dollars (through t-1). Buy early if above zero, else buy late.
expect: RATIO near the sugar rule (+0.34) if the Brazil factor is the cause.

hypothesis: The market adds a frost-risk premium before the Brazilian winter (frost season Jun-Aug) and removes it when the winter passes. Prices tend to rise from February to May and to fall from June to September.
change: Unfitted three-state calendar rule, no data: buy early in Feb-May, buy late in Jun-Sep, steady in Oct-Jan.
expect: RATIO above zero in both halves. Independent of all other signals.

hypothesis: Falsification test. If Brazil season heat is crop news, the same measure from regions with other crop calendars must have no skill. If it has the same skill, the signal is a climate clock, not crop news.
change: c21 with the Brazil nodes replaced by the 31 nodes of the other origins (simple mean): season-to-date maximum temperature, Oct-Apr, minus the last 5 years. Same sign rule.
expect: RATIO near zero if the Brazil signal is specific. A value near +0.5 would speak against the mechanism.

hypothesis: The volume of green coffee that Brazil exports shows how much coffee reaches the world market. A flow above the seasonal normal means ample supply and lower prices later; a low flow means a tight market.
change: Unfitted rule on one alt-data feature from new source 19: log of Brazil green-coffee export volume, mean of 3 months, minus the same months of the last 5 years (used from the 15th of the next month). Buy late if above normal, else buy early.
expect: RATIO above zero. Weak-to-medium prior: exports also react to the price.

hypothesis: Hedging-pressure theory: when producers and merchants hold a large net short hedge, the market pays a premium to those who take the other side, so futures prices tend to rise; a small hedge means no premium.
change: Unfitted three-state rule on one alt-data feature (CFTC, on hand): producer/merchant net short share of open interest, z-score against the last 104 reports. z > +1: buy early. z < -1: buy late. Else steady.
expect: RATIO above zero. It is close to the mirror of iteration 7, so a value near +0.1 is probable.

hypothesis: World growth and risk appetite move all commodities: strong demand and fund inflows lift prices. Equities, copper and crude oil show this state earlier and with less noise than coffee.
change: Vote of 3 market features: 126-session log return > 0 for the S&P 500, copper and crude oil (through t-1). Two or more rising: buy early, else buy late.
expect: RATIO near the other market-trend rules (+0.2 to +0.3).

hypothesis: If crop news enters the price slowly, the price already moves in the direction of the news. When the weather rule and the recent price move disagree, the market does not accept the news and the call is weak.
change: c22 with a price confirmation: keep the c22 position only when the 63-session coffee return has the same sign; else steady.
expect: Fewer active days. RATIO above c22 if slow adjustment is the mechanism.

hypothesis: A season-heat anomaly near zero is noise; a large anomaly is clear crop news. Acting only on large anomalies must raise the quality of the calls.
change: c21 with a dead zone: buy early if the season maximum-temperature anomaly is in the upper third of its earlier values (training rows of each test year), buy late in the lower third, else steady.
expect: Active on about two thirds of days. RATIO above c21 (+0.596) if size matters.

hypothesis: The market-trend rules are noisy views of one common factor (Brazil and world demand, dollar, funds). A vote of five different markets removes the noise of each one.
change: Vote of 5 market features: sugar, Brazil equities, copper (126-session return > 0), dollar index (63-session return < 0), coffee (252-session return > 0). Three or more: buy early, else buy late.
expect: RATIO about +0.3 to +0.4 with similar halves.

hypothesis: Weather (supply news) and the market-trend factor are independent. c28 used sugar alone for the trend; the five-market composite is the more reliable measure of the same factor.
change: c28 with the sugar trend replaced by the five-market vote of c42: position = sign(weather position of c22 + trend vote as +1/-1).
expect: RATIO near c28 (+0.576) with balanced halves.

hypothesis: Heat at flowering (Sep-Nov) makes flowers abort and fixes the number of fruits. If this is the main channel, flowering heat alone carries the signal and is known months earlier than the full season.
change: c21 with the window Sep-Nov only: mean maximum temperature of the flowering months to date, held until the next September, minus the last 5 years. Same sign rule.
expect: RATIO above zero; near c21 (+0.596) if flowering is the main channel.

hypothesis: Heat at grain fill (Jan-Mar) reduces bean size and weight. c44 showed that flowering heat alone has no stable skill. If the fill months carry the signal, this window alone must score like the full season.
change: c21 with the window Jan-Mar only: mean maximum temperature of the grain-fill months to date, held until the next January, minus the last 5 years. Same sign rule.
expect: RATIO near c21 (+0.596) if grain fill is the main channel.

hypothesis: c45 showed that the grain-fill months carry the heat signal. The c22 form (state of the crop and recent news must agree) with the grain-fill state must be equal or better and more equal over time.
change: c22 with the season heat (Oct-Apr) replaced by the grain-fill heat (Jan-Mar, held to the next January). Agreement with the 90-day stress as before.
expect: RATIO equal to or above c22 with more equal halves.

hypothesis: Grain-fill heat (state of the crop), 90-day stress (recent news) and the market-trend composite are three views with different mechanisms. A majority of the three is never without a call.
change: Majority of three signs: grain-fill maximum-temperature anomaly > 0, 90-day stress > 0, five-market trend vote positive. Two or three: buy early, else buy late.
expect: RATIO near +0.6 with equal halves.

hypothesis: Robustness of c45: grain-fill heat is a slow state, so weather data that are 10 days old must give nearly the same result.
change: c45 with the weather lag changed from 4 to 10 days.
expect: RATIO within 0.1 of c45 (+0.596).

hypothesis: Robustness of c45: the result must not depend on the length of the normal.
change: c45 with a 10-year normal in place of 5 years.
expect: RATIO within 0.15 of c45 (+0.596).

hypothesis: Robustness of c45: if grain-fill heat is real, the window one month earlier (Dec-Feb) must also show skill, a little less.
change: c45 with the window Dec-Feb (held to the next December).
expect: RATIO above +0.3.

hypothesis: Robustness of c45: if grain-fill heat is real, the window one month later (Feb-Apr) must also show skill.
change: c45 with the window Feb-Apr (held to the next February).
expect: RATIO above +0.3.

hypothesis: Robustness of c45: if heat is the cause, the daily mean temperature must show nearly the same skill as the daily maximum.
change: c45 with the daily mean temperature in place of the daily maximum temperature.
expect: RATIO within 0.15 of c45 (+0.596).

hypothesis: Robustness of c45: Minas Gerais grows most Brazilian arabica. The rule with the three Minas regions only must give nearly the same result.
change: c45 with the three Minas Gerais regions only (Sul de Minas, Matas de Minas, Cerrado Mineiro; weights re-scaled).
expect: RATIO within 0.15 of c45 (+0.596).

hypothesis: Holding coffee stocks costs interest. Rising US yields make traders and roasters cut stocks and make financial buyers leave commodities, so prices weaken; falling yields support prices.
change: Unfitted rule on one market feature: 126-session change of the log US 10-year yield (through t-1). Buy late if yields rose, else buy early.
expect: RATIO above zero. Weak prior; independent of weather.

hypothesis: Vietnam grows about 40% of world robusta. Heat in its dry season (Jan-Apr: flowering and fruit set) lowers the robusta crop; roasters then need more arabica, and the arabica price follows robusta up.
change: Unfitted rule on one alt-data feature (new data: NASA POWER, 3 Vietnamese regions): mean maximum temperature of Jan-Apr to date, held to the next January, minus the last 5 years, at t-4 days. Buy early if above normal, else buy late.
expect: RATIO above zero. Independent of Brazil weather.

hypothesis: Brazilian growers decide in reais. When the coffee price in reais is high against the last year they sell stocks and hedge the next crop, which presses the dollar price; when it is low they hold back.
change: Unfitted rule on one market feature: log(coffee price x USD/BRL) minus its 252-session mean. Buy late if above the mean, else buy early.
expect: RATIO above zero. Risk: value rules had the opposite sign in this market (c04, c25).

hypothesis: The four rules with skill use only signs. A logistic model fitted on earlier years can weight the signals by their strength and use their size.
change: Model change: logistic regression (C = 1, scaled) on 4 features: grain-fill mean-temperature anomaly, 90-day stress, Vietnam dry-season heat, number of rising markets (0-5). Buy early if probability > 0.5, else late.
expect: RATIO above the first logistic model (c15, +0.31). Above +0.6 would justify fitted weights.

hypothesis: The relations between these signals and the price change over the years. A model that gives old years less weight can follow the relation that holds now.
change: c57 with time-decay weights in the fit: a training row 3 years older than the newest row has half its weight. Same 4 features, same logistic regression.
expect: RATIO above c57 (+0.02) if the relations move slowly; near zero if there is no usable relation.

hypothesis: When equity-market fear (VIX) is high, funds cut risk and sell commodity positions; when fear is low they add risk. Coffee follows these flows.
change: Unfitted rule on one market feature: log VIX (through t-1) minus its 252-session mean. Buy late if above the mean, else buy early.
expect: RATIO above zero; weak prior.

hypothesis: Only two signals were stable in the two halves: the five-market trend composite and the Vietnam dry-season heat. They have different mechanisms (demand and funds; robusta supply). A rule from stable signals is more likely to hold outside the development years.
change: Agreement of two signals: five-market trend vote (c42) and Vietnam dry-season heat (c55). Both positive: buy early. Both negative: buy late. Else steady.
expect: RATIO about +0.4 with equal halves.

hypothesis: Colombia is the second arabica origin. A weakening peso raises the local price and makes Colombian growers and exporters sell, which presses the dollar price; a strengthening peso does the opposite.
change: Unfitted rule on one market feature: 63-session log return of USD/COP (through t-1). Buy late if above zero (peso weaker), else buy early.
expect: RATIO above zero; low prior after the USD/BRL result (c14, +0.07).

hypothesis: Roasters substitute between robusta and arabica. When the robusta price rises, blends move to arabica and the arabica price follows with a delay.
change: Unfitted rule on one market feature: 3-month log change of the World Bank monthly robusta price (used from the 15th of the next month). Buy early if above zero, else buy late.
expect: RATIO above zero with similar halves, like the Vietnam heat rule.

hypothesis: Volatility is predictable and the mean saving of a signal is not higher when volatility is high. Less exposure in high-volatility periods raises the saving for each unit of risk (volatility-managed exposure).
change: c22 with a volatility switch: steady when the 21-session log volatility of coffee returns is above the upper-third limit of the training rows; else the c22 position.
expect: RATIO above c22 (+0.612) by 0.05 to 0.15; fewer active days.

hypothesis: A positive Indian Ocean Dipole brings drought to Indonesia and floods to East Africa. Both reduce coffee supply from origins that the Brazil and Vietnam rules do not cover.
change: Unfitted three-state rule on one alt-data feature (NOAA Dipole Mode Index, used from the 15th of month M+2): index above +0.4: buy early. Below -0.4: buy late. Else steady.
expect: RATIO above zero; low prior after two ENSO failures.

hypothesis: Robustness of the market-trend factor (c42): a real common trend must also show with a shorter horizon.
change: c42 with a 63-session horizon for all five markets (sugar, Brazil equities, copper, dollar reversed, coffee). Three or more positive: buy early, else buy late.
expect: RATIO above +0.2 with the same sign in the two halves.

hypothesis: Robustness of the market-trend factor (c42): if slow trends carry it, a 252-session horizon for all markets must keep or raise the score.
change: c42 with a 252-session horizon for all five markets. Three or more positive: buy early, else buy late.
expect: RATIO near c42 (+0.34).

hypothesis: Colombia is the second arabica origin. Its main crop flowers in January-March; heat in that window reduces the harvest of October-December, and the market learns the loss slowly.
change: Unfitted rule on one alt-data feature: mean maximum temperature of Jan-Mar to date over the 6 Colombian nodes, held to the next January, minus the last 5 years. Buy early if above normal, else buy late.
expect: RATIO above zero with similar halves, like the Vietnam rule (+0.24).

hypothesis: Falsification test. In Central America and Mexico, January-March is harvest time and heat then has little effect on the crop. If Jan-Mar heat there scores like Brazil and Colombia, the signal is a common tropical warmth (a clock), not crop news.
change: Same rule as c67 with the 14 nodes of Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua and Mexico: mean maximum temperature of Jan-Mar to date, held to the next January, minus the last 5 years.
expect: RATIO near zero if the Brazil and Colombia signals are crop news; near +0.5 if they are a clock.

hypothesis: If Brazilian grain-fill heat is crop news, the part of it that is NOT shared with the other tropical regions must carry skill. If only the common warmth matters, the Brazil-specific part has none.
change: Unfitted rule on one alt-data feature: Brazil Jan-Mar maximum-temperature anomaly minus the same anomaly of the 31 other nodes (both against the last 5 years, held to the next January). Buy early if Brazil is hotter than the common anomaly, else buy late.
expect: RATIO above +0.3 if Brazil crop news is real; near zero if the common warmth is the signal.

hypothesis: The common January-March warmth of the tropical coffee regions outside Brazil. If the heat finding is mostly a common climate state, this measure alone must score like the Brazil rule.
change: Unfitted rule on one alt-data feature: Jan-Mar maximum-temperature anomaly of the 31 nodes outside Brazil (against the last 5 years, held to the next January). Buy early if above normal, else buy late.
expect: RATIO between the Central America test (+0.33) and Colombia (+0.51).

hypothesis: El Nino in the northern winter brings heat and drought to Colombia, Central America, Vietnam and Indonesia. Supply outside Brazil falls in the following harvests and the price rises in that year; La Nina does the opposite.
change: Unfitted rule on one alt-data feature: Nino 3.4 anomaly of January (published mid February), held until the next January value. Above zero: buy early. Below zero: buy late.
expect: RATIO near the common-warmth rule (c70, +0.42) if that warmth is ENSO.

hypothesis: Three weak signals with different causes: ENSO winter state (supply outside Brazil), Brazil-specific grain-fill heat (supply in Brazil), slow market trend (demand and funds). If they are independent, a majority of the three is stronger than each one.
change: Majority of three signs: Nino 3.4 of January > 0; Brazil Jan-Mar heat anomaly minus the other regions > 0; five-market trend vote positive. Two or three: buy early, else buy late.
expect: RATIO about +0.5 to +0.65 with equal halves.

hypothesis: c72 with the stronger Brazil measure. The full grain-fill heat (c52) scored +0.68 alone; it shares its common part with the ENSO vote, so the vote may gain less than the single scores suggest.
change: c72 with the Brazil-specific heat replaced by the full Brazil Jan-Mar mean-temperature anomaly (c52). Majority of that, Nino 3.4 of January, and the five-market trend vote.
expect: RATIO at or above c72 (+0.572).

hypothesis: The supply effect comes from real El Nino and La Nina events. In neutral winters the small sign of the index has no physical meaning and adds noise.
change: c71 as a three-state rule: January Nino 3.4 above +0.5: buy early. Below -0.5: buy late. Between: steady. Held until the next January value.
expect: RATIO at or above c71 (+0.385) with fewer active years.

hypothesis: ENSO winter state (supply outside Brazil) and slow market trend (demand and funds) are the two signals with the most stable record and with different causes. A rule from these two does not use Brazil weather, which failed before 2009.
change: Agreement of two signals: Nino 3.4 of January (sign) and the five-market trend vote. Both positive: buy early. Both negative: buy late. Else steady.
expect: RATIO about +0.5 with equal halves.

hypothesis: A depth-2 decision tree on the three inputs of c73 is a fitted version of the vote: it can find the thresholds and the one interaction that the earlier years support, and it stays readable.
change: Model change: decision tree (depth 2, at least 200 rows in a leaf) on 3 features: January Nino 3.4, Brazil Jan-Mar mean-temperature anomaly, number of rising markets (0-5). Buy early if probability > 0.5, else late.
expect: RATIO below the unfitted vote c73 (+0.646); above +0.3 would be a good result for a fitted model.

hypothesis: Data check: if Brazil grain-fill heat is a real weather state, an independent reanalysis (ERA5, ECMWF) must give nearly the same signal as NASA POWER (MERRA-2).
change: c52 with ERA5 daily mean temperature (new source 18, at t-7 days) in place of the NASA POWER temperature. Same nodes, weights, window and normal.
expect: RATIO within 0.15 of c52 (+0.680).

hypothesis: The climatic water balance (rain minus reference evapotranspiration) is the physical measure of drought stress: it joins rain and heat. If water stress is the cause of the crop loss, the water balance of the grain-fill months must score at least like heat alone.
change: Unfitted rule on one alt-data feature (ERA5, t-7 days): Brazil output-weighted mean of (rain - ET0) over Jan-Mar to date, held to the next January, minus the last 5 years. Buy early if below normal (drier), else buy late.
expect: RATIO near c77 (+0.447) if water stress is the cause; clearly lower means that the signal is temperature.

hypothesis: Robustness of c73: its two weather inputs are yearly states, so weather data that are 10 days old must give the same result.
change: c73 with the weather lag of the Brazil heat changed from 4 to 10 days.
expect: RATIO within 0.1 of c73 (+0.646).

hypothesis: Robustness of c73: with the independent ERA5 temperature in place of NASA POWER, the vote must keep most of its score.
change: c73 with the Brazil Jan-Mar mean-temperature anomaly from ERA5 (t-7 days) in place of NASA POWER.
expect: RATIO above +0.5.

hypothesis: Robustness of c73: the market factor is a slow trend (c66). With 252-session trends for all five markets the vote must keep its score and change position less often.
change: c73 with the five-market trend vote computed from 252-session returns (as in c66).
expect: RATIO within 0.1 of c73 (+0.646).

hypothesis: Robustness of c73: an ENSO event is defined by a season, not by one month. The December-February mean (known in mid March) must give nearly the same vote as the January value.
change: c73 with the January Nino 3.4 value replaced by the December-February mean (available from mid March, held to the next March).
expect: RATIO within 0.1 of c73 (+0.646).

hypothesis: Ablation of c73: the two yearly climate states alone (ENSO winter state and Brazil grain-fill heat). The difference to c73 is the value of the market-trend vote.
change: Agreement of two signals: January Nino 3.4 (sign) and Brazil Jan-Mar mean-temperature anomaly (sign). Both positive: buy early. Both negative: buy late. Else steady.
expect: RATIO below c73; about +0.5.

hypothesis: Robustness of c83: the December-February ENSO mean (known mid March) in place of the January value.
change: c83 with the January Nino 3.4 value replaced by the December-February mean.
expect: RATIO within 0.1 of c83 (+0.705).

hypothesis: Robustness of c83: with the independent ERA5 temperature in place of NASA POWER the rule must keep most of its score.
change: c83 with the Brazil Jan-Mar mean-temperature anomaly from ERA5 (t-7 days).
expect: RATIO above +0.5; the ERA5 heat rule alone gave +0.45 against +0.68.

hypothesis: Robustness of c83: both inputs are yearly states, so weather data that are 10 days old must give the same result.
change: c83 with the weather lag of the Brazil heat changed from 4 to 10 days.
expect: RATIO within 0.1 of c83 (+0.705).

hypothesis: Check of c86: the daily maximum temperature in place of the daily mean must give nearly the same rule.
change: c86 with the Brazil Jan-Mar maximum-temperature anomaly in place of the mean-temperature anomaly.
expect: RATIO within 0.15 of c86 (+0.787).

hypothesis: Check of c86: a 10-year normal in place of the 5-year normal.
change: c86 with the Brazil heat anomaly measured against the last 10 years.
expect: RATIO within 0.15 of c86 (+0.787).

hypothesis: Check of c86: the three Minas Gerais regions only (74% of the weight).
change: c86 with the Brazil heat anomaly from Sul de Minas, Matas de Minas and Cerrado Mineiro only.
expect: RATIO within 0.15 of c86 (+0.787).

hypothesis: Check of c86: the Brazil heat window one month earlier (Dec-Feb, held to the next December).
change: c86 with the Brazil heat window Dec-Feb in place of Jan-Mar.
expect: RATIO above +0.5.

hypothesis: Check of c86: the Brazil heat anomaly contains the common ENSO warmth. With the Brazil-specific part only (Brazil minus the other regions), the rule shows what Brazil adds to the ENSO state.
change: c86 with the Brazil heat anomaly replaced by the Brazil-specific anomaly (Brazil Jan-Mar maximum-temperature anomaly minus that of the 31 other nodes, lag 10 days).
expect: RATIO between the ENSO rule alone (+0.39) and c86 (+0.79).

hypothesis: Falsification of c86: if the second input only has to be a warm tropical first quarter, the Jan-Mar heat of Central America and Mexico (no crop meaning in those months) will work as well as the Brazil heat.
change: c86 with the Brazil heat anomaly replaced by the Jan-Mar maximum-temperature anomaly of the 14 nodes of Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua and Mexico (lag 10 days).
expect: RATIO clearly below c86 (+0.787) if Brazil is special; near it if not.

hypothesis: The rule depends on the weather product (NASA POWER +0.79, ERA5 +0.50). The two products measure the same heat with different errors; their mean has less error than each one.
change: c86 with the Brazil heat anomaly replaced by the mean of the NASA POWER and ERA5 anomalies (each scaled by its own earlier standard deviation; lag 10 days).
expect: RATIO between the two single-product versions (+0.50 and +0.79); this is the honest size of the rule.

hypothesis: A call with three independent reasons (ENSO state, Brazil heat, market trend) is more reliable than a call with two. Acting only on full agreement trades active days for quality.
change: c86 plus the five-market trend vote as a third condition: buy early only if all three are positive, buy late only if all three are negative, else steady.
expect: Fewer active days; RATIO near c86 only if the trend vote removes bad calls.

hypothesis: Check of c86 with another origin: Vietnam dry-season heat has crop meaning for robusta. If the second input must be Brazilian supply news, Vietnam heat will add little to the ENSO state.
change: c86 with the Brazil heat anomaly replaced by the Vietnam Jan-Apr maximum-temperature anomaly (3 robusta regions, lag 10 days).
expect: RATIO between the ENSO rule alone (+0.39) and c86 (+0.79).

hypothesis: Colombia flowering heat scored +0.51 alone. If that came from the ENSO state (El Nino heats Colombia in the first quarter), Colombia heat will add nothing to the ENSO state.
change: c86 with the Brazil heat anomaly replaced by the Colombia Jan-Mar maximum-temperature anomaly (6 nodes, lag 10 days).
expect: RATIO near the ENSO rule alone (+0.39) if Colombia heat is ENSO.

hypothesis: Check of c86: the supply effect of ENSO comes from real events. With neutral winters set to steady, the rule acts only when a real El Nino or La Nina agrees with the Brazil heat.
change: c86 with the ENSO condition as an event: January Nino 3.4 above +0.5 and Brazil heat above normal: buy early; below -0.5 and Brazil heat below normal: buy late; else steady.
expect: Fewer active years; RATIO near c86 if the events carry the effect.

hypothesis: An ENSO event can start or end in the middle of the year. A January value that is 7 to 12 months old can be wrong for the second half; the July value (published mid August) is a fresher state.
change: c86 with the ENSO input updated two times a year: the January value from mid February and the July value from mid August.
expect: RATIO at or above c86 if the fresher state helps; lower if only the winter state matters.

hypothesis: The design for a buyer, with the two choices that do not depend on luck: ENSO as the standard December-February mean (known mid March) and the Brazil January-March heat as the mean of two independent weather products.
change: Agreement of two signals: December-February Nino 3.4 mean (sign) and the two-product Brazil Jan-Mar heat anomaly (sign). Both positive: buy early. Both negative: buy late. Else steady.
expect: RATIO about +0.6 (c93 gave +0.599 with the January ENSO value).

hypothesis: The careful design with a third, independent view: the slow market trend. A majority of three is always active.
change: Majority of three signs: December-February Nino 3.4 mean, two-product Brazil Jan-Mar heat anomaly, five-market trend vote. Two or three positive: buy early, else buy late.
expect: RATIO about +0.55 to +0.65 (the c73 design with the careful inputs).
